# Packaged MCP startup and guidance

Windows executable acceptance now starts the package's actual MCP entrypoint with its bundled Node executable. A fixed protocol initializes `arcane-studio`, compares its complete tool inventory with the package's reviewed `ARCANE_TOOL_NAMES`, then calls the local `skills_recommend` tool. The response must contain bounded, unique skill identities, nonblank guidance and matching text/structured evidence. Existing skill checksums, declared status and approval policy remain in force.

The probe supplies a fresh dummy bearer only through its sanitized child environment. Its daemon URL points to a private rejecting loopback listener; successful verification requires zero requests to that listener. The fixed protocol sends no Studio, asset, provider or mutation call. The working directory is a fresh owned verification directory, while guidance comes from the actual bundled registry. A regression places a decoy registry in the working directory and still exercises bundled guidance.

The owned process has a 15-second deadline, a 256 KiB individual-message buffer, a 512 KiB total stdout limit and a 16 KiB diagnostic limit. Successful verification requires all three protocol responses, exact inventory, validated guidance, empty diagnostics, no trailing partial message and actual terminal exit code 0 with no signal. Returning the last response alone cannot satisfy shutdown. Failure terminates only the original owned child and waits for terminal acknowledgement; missing acknowledgement is retained as uncertainty. Reports contain counts, timings, exit state and diagnostic hashes rather than bearer or guidance contents. Listener shutdown starts before force-closing its connections.

`check-windows-executable.mjs` retains `mcp-runtime.json` beside its existing executable reports and adds three checks: `mcpProtocolVerified`, `bundledGuidanceVerified` and `mcpShutdownVerified`. It continues to verify the bundle inventory before and after execution, run the isolated desktop/daemon smoke and exercise independent parent-loss shutdown.

The production entrypoint regression belongs to the compiled unit inventory. Standalone protocol/process fixtures remain in the release inventory, so they require no compiled product tree. Together with the existing executable process-helper suite, the focused inventory covers malformed response IDs, duplicate tool names, oversized output, invalid guidance, invalid/duplicate skill identities, blank context, trailing output, nonzero exit, diagnostics, unexpected daemon requests, a stalled request and a child that remains alive after its final response.

Validation passed with 270 compiled sources and 24/24 focused cases, zero failures or skips (34.171 seconds). Logs are `runtime/mcp-runtime-build.log` and `runtime/mcp-runtime-final-tests.log`. Independent source review covered protocol correlation, process exit, listener cleanup, evidence bounds and report privacy.

The final verifier ran against the preserved main-`f6ad63c` Windows bundle `runtime/windows/arcane-win32-x64-LPcJ4S`, whose manifest remains `47744913a4290acc85a6c85e06e7f89143e78035a3733384b9dfefcef44410b9`. All 30 checks passed with terminal exit 0 and unchanged before/after bundle inventories. MCP discovery returned all 29 expected tools, loaded bundled guidance in 826 ms, emitted no diagnostics, made zero daemon requests and exited 0. The full verifier took 62,154 ms. Evidence is retained in `runtime/verification/windows-executable-j2k3IX/verification.json`, `mcp-runtime.json` and `runtime/mcp-windows-final-verification.log`. This records the external verifier's completed checks against the existing package; the package's own source snapshot remains the original main commit.

This verification covers the packaged local command surface and bundled guidance. Provider authentication, inference, native Studio behavior and customer gameplay acceptance retain their own evidence requirements; `fullProductVerified` remains false.
